newsitem.title: UK: Jordan's King Hussein to discuss Iraq with Blair.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's King Hussein to discuss Iraq with Blair.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein will meet Prime Minister Tony Blair on Thursday for talks on a looming crisis with Iraq as well as the stalled Middle East peace process, officials said on Tuesday.

Diplomats and analysts say Iraqi President Saddam Hussein could soon trigger another showdown with the United Nations after the Security Council on Saturday threatened Baghdad with more sanctions unless it stopped obstructing U.N. arms inspectors.
"It is important that Jordan continues to maintain solidarity with those nations opposed to Saddam Hussein," a Foreign Office spokesman said by telephone.
"We are all still waiting for a change in Iraqi behaviour so the sanctions can be dropped."

King Hussein distanced himself from Saddam by openly calling for a change in government in Baghdad after sheltering senior defectors in 1995 but ties between the two neighbours are gradually improving.
Last week Iraqi newspapers said a senior Jordanian official had began talks with an Iraqi oil official to boost cooperation.
The two countries signed an oil deal in January whereby Iraq agreed to supply Amman with 4.5 million tonnes of crude oil and refined oil products in 1997.

In December the United Nations allowed Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months ending in June to finance the purchase of medical and other goods. The deal has been renewed for another six months.
But before all the sanctions are removed the U.N. inspectors must certify that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction.

Chief weapons inspector Rolf Ekeus complained in Janaury of feeble support from the Security Council and some inspectors fear that the major powers want to relax sanctions so they can conclude lucrative trade deals with Iraq.
Last week Syria opened its borders to Iraq for the first time in 15 years.
The British spokesman said Blair and King Hussein would also discuss the Middle East peace process, which is currently deadlocked.
Talks between Israel and the Palestinians broke down in March when the Jewish state began building a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
